🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system (degraded mode — no Slack MCP, DD monitor scan-diff)  •  bug-type guess: unknown  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Integrations` (`@integrations` / `#team-integrations`)

Symptoms:
  - eda_consumer's outbound HTTP calls to ms-preferences-api failed almost completely (94 errors, up to 100% error rate) for ~2.5 min (12:28:00-12:30:30Z)
  - ms-preferences-api's own server-side error/hit metrics show zero disruption throughout — this is a client-side/network-path failure, not ms-preferences-api rejecting requests
  - Self-recovered by 12:30:30Z; monitor's rolling 10-min eval window didn't flip to Alert until 12:41:52Z (known eval-lag pattern)
  - Overturns the prior (2026-07-24) hypothesis that this monitor measures external customer-webhook failures — this fire's `by {peer.service}` breakdown pins the dependency as the internal ms-preferences-api, not a customer endpoint

Trace IDs: none indexed (client-side connection failures, 0 hits on service:eda_consumer status:error logs)
Likely cause: Transient connectivity failure (DNS/connection-pool/service-discovery) between eda_consumer and ms-preferences-api. Root cause not pinned down.
Suggested next action: file defect — track eda_consumer -> ms-preferences-api dependency fragility; watch for recurrence with same peer.service signature

  • DD metric (ms-preferences-api server errors, confirms 0): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request.errors&exp_scope=service%3Ams-preferences-api%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=sum&start=1785500700&end=1785501900

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 7)
Channel: alert-system (degraded mode — no Slack MCP, DD monitor scan-diff)  •  bug-type guess: unknown  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)

Symptoms:
  - tables-fields p95 request latency spiked to 0.87s (vs 0.25s threshold) at 12:47:20Z, elevated ~12:46:10-12:50:00Z, self-recovered
  - Request volume jumped ~80x baseline (from ~3-5 req/10s to ~400 req/10s) during the same window, spread broadly across HealthCheckController, GetFieldNamesWithRestriction, GetFieldNamesAndTypesFriendly, ViewController.GetViewBasicInfo/GetViewNames — not one runaway caller
  - This monitor's established KB entry (Redis Cache Circuit Breaker) does NOT apply this time: 0 hits on its own ES evidence_query, 0 Redis command errors on tables-fields throughout the window
  - 2 unrelated InvalidViewName exceptions (view names "ContactType", "Status") logged in the same window on /v1/field/SaveViewBundleInternal — same ActionId, doesn't explain the service-wide traffic spike by itself
  - Fired 4 seconds before monitor 227940275 (Redis Errors) — investigated for a shared cause; none found, that monitor's errors trace to an unrelated service (nonprod/apps mobile relay)

Trace IDs: n/a (no single representative trace pulled — this is a volume/aggregate signature, not a single failing request)
Likely cause: Unexplained ~80x request-volume burst against tables-fields (health-check + field/view metadata traffic), self-recovering in ~4 min. Source of the burst not identified — no per-account concentration signal, no app-update push-storm signature, no Redis involvement.
Suggested next action: file defect — track as a distinct tables-fields latency mechanism from the known Redis-circuit-breaker pattern; monitor for recurrence to identify the calling process
